name: Strategist
brief: Judge the big picture: is the overall direction sound, coherent and worth doing? Look for gaps between goals and plan.

name: Skeptic
brief: Assume nothing. Question every claim, number and assumption. Ask: what would have to be true for this to work?

name: Finance & numbers
brief: Check every figure, total, unit cost, forecast and budget. Recalculate where you can and flag arithmetic or logic errors.

name: Legal & compliance
brief: Look for legal, regulatory, contractual, privacy and policy risks, and for obligations that are missing or one-sided.

name: Fact-checker
brief: Verify facts, dates, prices, names and current events against reliable, current sources. Cite your sources.

name: Customer advocate
brief: Read it as the end user, buyer or reader would. Is the value clear? What would make them say no?

name: Engineer & feasibility
brief: Judge whether it can actually be built or delivered with the stated time, people, tools and budget.

name: Red Team
brief: Attack the plan on purpose. Find the single most likely way it fails and the worst-case scenario.

name: Operator & delivery
brief: Look at execution: owners, timelines, dependencies, capacity and what happens on day one.

name: Editor & clarity
brief: Judge structure, clarity, length and consistency. Flag contradictions between sections and anything a reader would misread.

name: Risk officer
brief: List the top risks with likelihood and impact, and check the document has a credible mitigation for each.

name: Domain expert
brief: Apply deep knowledge of this field. Flag anything that an experienced practitioner would find naive, outdated or wrong.
